1.why: All seven screens show a static, clean layout with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary headings and the blue action buttons stand out clearly against the white cards and light background.

3.why: Each step presents a single focused form so the needed field and button are immediately visible.

4.why: The user must recall and re-enter long tokens and codes across multiple distinct steps without persistent cues on the form itself.

5.why: No password-manager hints, autofill attributes, or “remember me” options appear on any screen.

6.why: Aside from the logs panel showing prior values, the forms themselves offer no recognizable saved or familiar items.

7.why: Labels and instructions are short, use plain language, and are easy to read.

8.why: No error messages or validation feedback are shown in any of the provided screenshots.

9.why: Password rules are stated and the logs show example tokens/codes, but the input fields themselves lack inline examples or placeholders.

10.why: The flow offers only password reset and code entry; no alternative choices such as face login or other methods are presented.

11.why: Each screen contains exactly one primary task and at most one or two fields, avoiding choice overload.

12.why: Success screens explicitly confirm outcomes (“Sign-in confirmed”, “Privacy conditions accepted”) and the logs record each completed action.

13.why: Brief instructional text appears on some steps, yet no contextual help links, tooltips, or short tips for new actions are provided.

14.why: Nothing prevents re-trying, but no explicit “try again” affordance or error-recovery guidance is visible.

15.why: Every screen re-uses the same header, card layout, button style, and warning banner, keeping the design consistent.
